Aircraft Activity
General Mitchell Field is expected to remain as the region's only scheduled air carrier airport and in addition serves the growing needs of commercial and business aircraft and general aviation.
Its runways accommodate modern jet aircraft, both commercial and military. It is equipped with the most modern navigational and landing aids. Facilities to serve the needs of commercial, corporate and private plane owners are also provided. The areas north and east of the airport are designated for general aviation. Corporate hangars are located to the southwest. The Air National Guard has facilities on the east side of the airport and the U.S. Air Force Reserve has substantial facilities adjacent to the airport on the southwest. Five of the nation's major airlines schedule over 120 daily flights with either direct or excellent connections available to all metropolitan centers, we well as Mexico, Nawaii, Alaska and the Orient. On February 1, 1974 regularly scheduled 747 jumbo jet service began between Milwaukee and New York. Two local service airlines also serve the airport.
The regional airport system plan, currently under preparation by SEURPC has listed growth forecasts of 5,038,000 to 5,597,000 passengers and 211,200 tons of air cargo in 1990. This compares favorably to the forecast by the Milwaukee County Airport Department of 5,400,000 total air passenger movements and 220,000 tons of air cargo shown in figure 14.
At the present time there are no plans to limit the number of aircraft operations at General Nitchell Field.
